title: Run the Dang Ball!
text:
We constantly hear in the crowds, “Run the dang ball!”
That statement is getting put to the test today when we look at last year’s results and how teams performed. We have seen throughout the years of football dominant teams who push the ball down the field with different types of run formations. Ranked third all-time in the most rushing yards in a season is the
Nebraska Cornhuskers with 4,820 yards on the ground. The one thing that makes that team so notable.. They could actually win.


Code
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(tidyverse)
library(ggrepel)
library(gt)
fbs <- read_csv("dat/fbs_2025_rushing_wins.csv") |>
  mutate(
    record_group = case_when(
      wins >= 10    ~ "Elite (10+ wins)",
      wins < losses ~ "Losing (more losses than wins)",
      wins >= losses ~ "Middle (.500 or better, under 10 wins)"
    )
  )
standouts <- filter(fbs, team %in% c("Navy", "Utah", "Air Force", "Army",
                                     "Jacksonville State", "Indiana", "Miami (FL)",
                                     "Oregon", "Ole Miss", "New Mexico State",
                                     "Alabama", "Ohio State", "Old Dominion", "Texas Tech"))
ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = fbs, aes(x = rush_ypg, y = wins), color = "#B8AE9C") +
  geom_smooth(data = fbs, aes(x = rush_ypg, y = wins), method = "lm", color = "#2B2B2B", se = FALSE) +
  geom_point(data = standouts, aes(x = rush_ypg, y = wins), color = "#E41C38", size = 2.5) +
  geom_text_repel(data = standouts, aes(x = rush_ypg, y = wins, label = team)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = mean(fbs$wins), color = "#8C8C8C") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean(fbs$rush_ypg), color = "#8C8C8C") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(70, 310)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-2, 19)) +
  geom_text(
    aes(x = 303, y = 7.8),
    label = "Avg. wins",
    size = 2.5,
    color = "#8C8C8C"
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(x = 180, y = 18),
    label = "Avg. rushing yards",
    size = 2.5,
    color = "#8C8C8C"
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(x = 105, y = 18),
    label = "Winning without the run",
    size = 3,
    color = "#2B2B2B"
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(x = 245, y = 18),
    label = "Running and winning",
    size = 3,
    color = "#E41C38",
    fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(x = 105, y = -1.5),
    label = "Neither running nor winning",
    size = 3,
    color = "#2B2B2B"
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(x = 245, y = -1.5),
    label = "Running but still losing",
    size = 3,
    color = "#2B2B2B"
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(x = 175, y = -1.5),
    label = "r = 0.45",
    size = 2.5,
    color = "#8C8C8C"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Teams that enjoy the run, tend to win",
    subtitle = "Rushing yards are very much connected to win... unless you are Air Force",
    x = "Rushing Yards per Game", y = "Wins",
    caption = "By: Gryphon Ferguson | Source: 2025 FBS season data"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", color = "#2B2B2B"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 8),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )









In 2025, Navy led the entire nation with 285.6 rushing yards per game, as you can see with them dominating. This team is a greeting show at how dominating the run can make winning the game so much easier. Navy was led by quarterback Blake Horvath and Alex Tecza. They combined for a total of 2,102 yards on the ground. Carrying Navy to their best record since 2019. Navy is a heavy rushing team, so let’s look at someone else like New Mexico State.
New Mexico State had the lowest average amount of yards rushed. Hence why they struggled to win any games this year. They have an established run game and were unable to remain competitive for the season.


Code
record_avg <- fbs |>
  group_by(record_group) |>
  summarise(teams = n(), avg_rush_ypg = mean(rush_ypg))
ggplot() +
  geom_bar(data = record_avg,
           aes(x = reorder(record_group, avg_rush_ypg),
               weight = avg_rush_ypg, fill = record_group)) +
  geom_text(data = record_avg,
            aes(x = reorder(record_group, avg_rush_ypg),
                y = avg_rush_ypg + 12, label = round(avg_rush_ypg, 1)),
            size = 4, color = "#2B2B2B") +
  geom_text(data = record_avg,
            aes(x = reorder(record_group, avg_rush_ypg),
                y = 12, label = teams),
            color = "white", size = 4) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 220)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Elite (10+ wins)" = "#E41C38",
                               "Middle (.500 or better, under 10 wins)" = "#8C8C8C",
                               "Losing (more losses than wins)" = "#2B2B2B")) +
  labs(
    title = "Elite teams rush for about 45 more yards\nper game than losing teams",
    subtitle = "Number outside each bar = average rushing yards per game\nWhite number inside each bar = number of teams",
    x = "Team Record Category",
    y = "Average Rushing Yards per Game",
    caption = "By: Gryphon Ferguson | Source: 2025 FBS season data"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", color = "#2B2B2B"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 8),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )









Only 25 times were able to win at least 10+ games to be considered an Elite team. The average amount of yards those teams ran for is 186.8. Showing that this is the general area that you need to be around to have success in games.
Strong run games equal more wins. Losing teams who struggle to gain any type of yardage on the run are normally sitting around 142.2 rushing yards per game.
57 teams fall in this category. 42% of college football teams were failing to run the ball. This led to those teams not having an established offense and led to them not winning.


Code
elite_offense <- fbs %>%
  filter(wins >= 10) %>%
  select(team, rush_ypg, def_ypg_allowed, wins, losses) %>%
  arrange(desc(rush_ypg))

elite_offense %>%
  gt() %>%
  cols_label(
    team = "Team",
    rush_ypg = "Rush YPG",
    def_ypg_allowed = "Yards Allowed YPG",
    wins = "Wins",
    losses = "Losses"
  ) %>%
  tab_header(
    title = "Most Elite Teams Ran the Ball, but a Few Won Without It",
    subtitle = "2025 FBS teams with 10+ wins. 20 out of the 25 rushed for more than the FBS average of 158 yards per game. Navy led the nation at 285.6, while Alabama won 11 games, with just 104.1."
  ) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(color = "#2B2B2B", weight = "bold", align = "left"),
    locations = cells_title("title")
  ) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(color = "#2B2B2B", align = "left"),
    locations = cells_title("subtitle")
  ) %>%
  tab_source_note(
    source_note = md("**By:** Gryphon Ferguson  |  **Source:** 2025 FBS season data")
  ) %>%
  tab_style(
    locations = cells_column_labels(columns = everything()),
    style = list(
      cell_borders(sides = "bottom", weight = px(3)),
      cell_text(weight = "bold", size = 12)
    )
  ) %>%
  opt_row_striping() %>%
  opt_table_lines("none") %>%
  fmt_number(
    columns = c(rush_ypg, def_ypg_allowed),
    decimals = 1
  ) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = list(
      cell_fill(color = "#00205B"),
      cell_text(color = "#FFFFFF")
    ),
    locations = cells_body(rows = team == "Navy")
  ) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = list(
      cell_fill(color = "#990000"),
      cell_text(color = "#FFFFFF")
    ),
    locations = cells_body(rows = team == "Indiana")
  ) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = list(
      cell_fill(color = "#9E1B32"),
      cell_text(color = "#FFFFFF")
    ),
    locations = cells_body(rows = team == "Alabama")
  )

Running the ball can mean so much for the control of the game and can even help bail out teams. Navy had a not-great defense, allowing just 371.3 yards on defense. Even with this fault. The run game was so powerful that it was able to propel them to an 11-2 record.
Now we have our teams that refuse to run the ball and are still an elite team. Alabama is a great example of a team that didn’t love the run but still was able to be competitive. Alabama had a decent defense with a high-power throwing offense, which helped them get to that point.
Wide receiver Ryan Williams and Germie Bernard combined for 1,551 yards in the air and 11 touchdowns. Even with that type of offensive power, Alabama was unable to win the big games, hence the 11-4 record.
So if you are mad that current-day Nebraska isn’t running the ball.. You should be… Teams that have a great understanding of the run game and know how to run it only win more games and have such great success.
